{{nihongo|'''Onouto Shrine'''|男乃宇刀神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumi Province]].

=== Enshrined deities ===
; Principal deities
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hikoitsuse-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188|lt=Kamuyamato-Iwarehiko-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Prince Inishikiirihiko|Q11372194|qid=Q11372194}}

=== History ===
In the name "Onouto," "Ono" means elder brother and "Uto" means younger brother, referring to enshrining elder brother {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hikoitsuse-no-Mikoto}} and younger brother {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188|lt=Kamuyamato-Iwarehiko-no-Mikoto}}. According to shrine tradition, when Hikoitsuse-no-Mikoto was wounded in battle with {{ill|Nagatsuhiko|Q4922278|qid=Q4922278}}, a local chieftain Yokoyama-hiko welcomed him here. It is an Engishiki shrine, and because of ties to the local ruler in the Genkei era, {{ill|Prince Inishikiirihiko|Q11372194|qid=Q11372194}} also came to be enshrined.

Two mikoshi descend the steep steps of the shrine building and circulate through the district<ref>''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Izumi City Fudoki (2)}}'', opening gravure (photos and commentary).</ref>.

* From {{ill|Izumi-Chūō Station (Osaka)|Q6102264|qid=Q6102264|lt=Izumi-Chuo Station}} on the {{ill|Semboku Line|Q2758012|qid=Q2758012}}, take Izumi City {{ill|route-maintenance bus|Q11279660|qid=Q11279660|lt=route-maintenance bus}} ({{ill|Chichioni route|Q11279660|qid=Q11279660|lt=Chichioni route}}) bound for "Makio Yamaguchi" or "Chichioni," get off at "Jinja-mae," immediately nearby.
* From Izumi-Chuo Station on the Nankai Semboku Line, take {{ill|Nankai Bus|Q11408154|qid=Q11408154}} {{ill|Sakamoto Line|Q11408155|qid=Q11408155|lt=Sakamoto Line}} or {{ill|Hatsugano Line|Q11408155|qid=Q11408155|lt=Hatsugano Line}}, get off at "Nobana" or "Izumi Aobadai," transfer to reservation shared-ride service "{{ill|Choisoko|Q107253531|qid=Q107253531}} Izumi," and get off at "704 Jinja-mae"<ref>
